subject: religious-studies
title: Does God Exist?
welcome_lead: Wrestle with one of humanity's oldest and biggest questions: is there a God?
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on philosophical arguments about God's existence.
final_note: You can now outline the main arguments for and against the existence of God.

concepts.def: Person who does not believe in any god.
Unsure if God exists or not.
Universe looks designed, so there must be a designer.
Everything has a cause, so the universe needs one.
Trust or belief without complete proof.

walkthroughs.body_html: The design argument says the universe is so complex and ordered that it must have a designer — God. The cosmological argument says everything has a cause, so there must be a 'first cause' — God. Many people also point to religious experience.

Atheists argue we have no scientific evidence for God, and that science (such as evolution and the Big Bang) can explain the universe without a creator. The problem of evil also challenges belief in a loving God.
An agnostic says we cannot know for sure whether God exists. They keep an open mind. Many people change between theism, atheism and agnosticism during their lives as they think and learn.

mcqs.q: What does karma mean in Hindu and Buddhist thought?
options: Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
The principle that actions have moral consequences shaping future experience or rebirth — not fate, but ethical cause and effect built into reality.
The Buddha created the universe.
Karma is when bad things happen to bad people as punishment.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
The Buddha created the universe.

mcqs.q: What does the term jihad mean in Islam?
options: Struggle or striving — the greater jihad is the internal spiritual struggle against sin; the lesser jihad refers to defensive military struggle under strict conditions.
Jihad means 'holy war' against non-Muslims.
Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
